clue.text: Epithalamium gets a similar green sort of union certificate

indicators.note: sort of suggests a loose version of the words a similar green, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wedding poem is turned, in a greenish way, into a document about a union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges A SIMILAR GREEN. 'Epithalamium' (a wedding poem) is a cryptic extra: such a poem is literally lines about a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the informal British name for the official document recording a wedding.

clue.text: Show, with grand girls, otherwise called Harmonica

parts.note: a musical is a stage show with songs
G is the usual abbreviation for grand (a thousand pounds or dollars)
lasses are girls, a northern British word

explanation.surface: A stage show with a wealthy cast of girls goes by another name.
explanation.walkthrough: The glass harmonica, Benjamin Franklin's instrument, is played by rubbing wet glass rims.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument of tuned glass bowls was also known as the glass harmonica.

clue.text: Summarize 11's revised version

indicators.note: a revised version of the cross-referenced answer has its letters set in a new order

parts.note: 11-across, whose solution is the word for a skip or a pickled flower bud, CAPER

explanation.surface: Summarize the reworked text of a previous item.
explanation.definitionFit: To recapitulate is to go over the main points again briefly.

clue.text: Meaning one without name or weight

definitions.meaning: meaning in the sense of significance
weight in the sense of influence or consequence

explanation.walkthrough: The middle, 'one without name or', paints someone who lacks exactly this quality: a nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonyms for significance, as in a matter of real consequence.

clue.text: Bottom of bag cut open -had a quick look

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter, here of bag

parts.note: to lance a boil is to cut it open

explanation.surface: Someone slit the base of a bag and peeked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to take a brief look, so the past tense means looked quickly.

clue.text: Word for word it's the compositor's fault

definitions.meaning: word for word means exact, a translation following the original closely
in printing a ... is a typographical slip, one wrong letter set by the typesetter

explanation.definitionFit: An exact rendering is called literal, and printers call a misprint a literal.

clue.text: Is said to be acquainted with an informer

indicators.note: is said tells us the word meaning acquainted is spoken, giving the sound of the answer

parts.note: to be acquainted with someone is to know them, so he knows

explanation.surface: Someone is reported to be friendly with a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a police informer a nose, one who sniffs out information.

clue.text: How Addison described himself in this periodical

definitions.text: How Addison described himself in this periodical

parts.words: How Addison described himself in this periodical
parts.note: Joseph Addison wrote his eighteenth-century daily essays in the persona of a silent onlooker, and the paper took that persona's name

explanation.walkthrough: Addison and Steele's essay paper of 1711 was narrated by a silent observer, Mr ..., who gave the paper its title.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker who watches without taking part gave the essay paper its name.

clue.text: Fiend in one of his 28, see — help stop him

indicators.note: 28 across means transformations, so the fiend appears in one of his changed shapes, the letters reshaped

explanation.surface: A devil in disguise; look out, and someone help stop him!
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one of his 28' (a shape-change, from 28-across) rearranges SEE and HELP STOP HIM.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the devil to whom Faust sells his soul, the archetypal demon.

clue.text: Toady's refusal to accept edited copy

indicators.note: to accept means the refusal word takes in the other letters

parts.note: shan't is a blunt refusal

indicators.note: edited copy is copy reworked, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flatterer will not take on rewritten text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges COPY to YCOP; 'to accept' puts that inside SHANT, the blunt refusal written without its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is a fawning flatterer, a servile hanger-on.

clue.text: A bit of a show of temperament?

definitions.text: A bit of a show of temperament?

parts.words: A bit of a show of temperament?
parts.note: reads as a small display of temper, but also as one division of a play

explanation.definitionFit: A play is divided into acts and these smaller parts, and a tantrum in public is also called this.

clue.text: Cut by the skipper? What sauce!

definitions.text: Cut by the skipper? What sauce!

parts.words: Cut by the skipper? What sauce!
parts.note: a skipper who leaps about cuts a frolicsome jump, and the pickled flower bud flavours a sauce

explanation.definitionFit: A playful leap is cut by someone dancing about, and pickled buds of the same name go into a sauce for fish.

clue.text: Denry Machin's diamond perhaps

definitions.meaning: Denry Machin is the cheeky, eccentric hero of an Arnold Bennett novel named after the kind of character he is
a diamond is one of the four suits in a pack used for bridge or whist

explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Bennett's novel The Card (1911) follows Denry Machin, a wag and chancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is a witty, eccentric person like Bennett's Denry, and a diamond is a playing suit.

clue.text: A hankering to join the Italian Church

parts.note: It is a standard abbreviation for Italian (as in It vermouth)

explanation.surface: Someone longs to become a member of the Catholic Church in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless desire, as in an itch to travel.

clue.text: Extremely aged man shows a lot of bottle

definitions.meaning: the patriarch in Genesis said to have lived 969 years
the name of a giant wine bottle holding eight standard bottles

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's oldest man lends his name to a huge champagne bottle.

clue.text: See doctor about pressure from this old money-lender

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold

indicators.note: about means the doctor letters are placed around the pressure word

parts.note: MD is Doctor of Medicine
a bar is a unit of pressure

explanation.surface: Behold, a doctor has been dealing with the pressure from a loan shark.
explanation.definitionFit: Lombards, bankers from northern Italy, were medieval pawnbrokers, remembered in London's Lombard Street.

clue.text: Peculiar behaviour in an old art style

definitions.meaning: the sixteenth-century Italian style after the High Renaissance, with elongated figures

explanation.definitionFit: A personal quirk of habit, and the Italian art movement following Michelangelo.

clue.text: To whom his father relates difficulties of borrowing and lending

definitions.text: To whom his father relates difficulties of borrowing and lending

indicators.note: difficulties suggests trouble with the word relates, which is jumbled

explanation.surface: Polonius warns his son about the pitfalls of loans: neither a borrower nor a lender be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficulties' rearranges RELATES. In Hamlet, Polonius advises his son 'Neither a borrower nor a lender be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonius's son in Hamlet receives that famous paternal advice about loans.

clue.text: Nothing turned out about origin of Chinese print

indicators.note: turned means the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil is nothing, zero

indicators.note: about means the word out goes around the start of the next word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: origin of means the first letter of Chinese

explanation.surface: A null result came out on the source of a Chinese engraving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses NIL to LIN; 'about' wraps OUT around C.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a print made from a design gouged into a linoleum block.

clue.text: A beam of light over the door

definitions.meaning: a horizontal crosspiece of wood or stone
a small window above a door, a fanlight

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crossbar and the window it supports above a doorway.

clue.text: 50% of school get wretched zero for music

indicators.note: 50% of means the first half of the six-letter word school
a wretched zero is in a bad state, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Half the school get a miserable zero for music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wretched' rearranges ZERO to ERZO. Half of the six-letter 'school' is its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively movement in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Help shoot a gull, say

indicators.note: say means the answer is heard as a word, not spelt like it

parts.note: a sucker is a shoot from a plant root, and also a gull, a dupe

explanation.surface: Help me bring down a seagull, I mean.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'shoot' and 'a gull' mean sucker; 'say' gives the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour is to give aid in hardship.

clue.text: Slough farm building perhaps

definitions.meaning: to slough is to cast off, as a snake its skin
a simple outbuilding, found on farms among other places

explanation.definitionFit: To cast off a skin, and a simple hut used for storage.

clue.text: Mineral extracted from metal containers

indicators.note: extracted from tells us letters are taken out of the run of metal containers

explanation.surface: A mineral is removed from tins.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral, magnesium silicate, ground for powder.

clue.text: Psalmist's direction put an end to 14

indicators.note: an end to the referenced word means only its closing part is kept, its start dropped

parts.note: 14-down, the patriarch who lived longest

explanation.surface: A psalm-writer's instruction finishes off an old man.
explanation.walkthrough: The last five letters of 14-down give the Hebrew word.
explanation.definitionFit: Selah is a Hebrew word in the Psalms, probably a direction to pause.

clue.text: Goes ahead with the roof-covering

definitions.meaning: the sheets of lead covering a roof

explanation.definitionFit: Being in front is leading, and lead sheets cover roofs.

clue.text: Sound measures of support for this achievement

indicators.note: sound means we hear the word for the measures, spelt differently

parts.note: feet are measures (twelve inches) and they support us

explanation.surface: Audible units of support account for this accomplishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is a notable deed or accomplishment.

clue.text: Able to return to where Napoleon suffered it

definitions.text: Able to return to where Napoleon suffered it

parts.words: Able to return to where Napoleon suffered it
parts.note: the word able read backwards spells Elba, the island where Napoleon was banished

explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was banished to Elba, a word that is able read backwards.

clue.text: A sort of pigeon dance? Some game!

parts.note: a stool pigeon is a decoy, so stool is a sort of pigeon
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A decoy bird does a dance: what a game!
explanation.walkthrough: Stoolball is an old English bat-and-ball game, ancestor of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old English sport played with bat and ball, still played in Sussex.

clue.text: Poet so hammers out transformations

indicators.note: out signals the words poet so hammers are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A poet hammers out changes of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges POET SO HAMMERS; the poet is Ovid, whose great poem bears this title.
explanation.definitionFit: It means changes of form, and is the title of Ovid's epic.
